**Affordability Crisis and Housing Costs**
Housing affordability has deteriorated significantly relative to wage growth since 2000. [Source: ev-2]
While median household income grew by only 92% during this period, home prices increased by 177% [Source: ev-2].
The Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024, representing a 225% increase since January 2000 [Source: ev-2].
Price-to-income ratios vary drastically by region; California cities show ratios between 9.6 and 12.2, which is more than double the national average of 4.7 [Source: ev-2].

**Economic Mobility**
The economic landscape is further complicated by worsening mobility for low-income families. [Source: ev-2]

Only Houston showed an improvement, with a 1.1% gain in income outcomes for those who grew up there [Source: ev-2].
